title: How to Turn Recipes Into One Grocery List
excerpt: Go from a suggested week of dinners to one linked shopping list, without copying ingredients by hand.
seoDescription: A practical way to turn multiple recipes into a single weekly grocery list without missed ingredients.
indexExcerpt: A practical recipe-to-list guide for creating one weekly grocery list.

sections.heading: Start with a suggested week
sections.body: On Home, choose Plan my week. In Plan your week, choose how many days you need, the start date and servings. Choose Plan my week there to generate suggestions, then review the dinners, swap unsuitable meals or leave a day free. You can try this without an account or a saved recipe collection.

sections.heading: Save the plan to create your list
sections.body: Choose Save my plan when the meals look right. If you are a guest, sign in or create an account at this point to keep the plan. Saving creates its shopping list automatically; there is no separate list-generation step.

sections.heading: Check your cupboards and add extras
sections.body: Open Shopping to review the ingredients from your saved plan. Check your cupboards lets you add suggested staples if you need them. Remove ingredients you already have, and add extras such as milk, foil or cleaning supplies. Foodedo does not track your pantry stock for you.

link.label: See the worked three-recipe shopping list, with quantities and source details.

sections.heading: Use the list while you shop
sections.body: Tick items off as you pick them up. Open an ingredient’s details to see which meals use it. If you change a meal in your saved plan, its linked list updates automatically. Manual extras stay, and checks on matching ingredients that are still needed are retained.

sections.heading: Make next week another small decision
sections.body: Think about which dinners worked before reviewing your next suggested week. Keep useful suggestions and swap the ones that do not fit. You do not need to rebuild a recipe collection to plan again.

title: How to Combine Ingredients From Multiple Recipes
excerpt: A straightforward way to combine ingredients from several meals into one weekly shop.
seoDescription: Learn how to combine recipe ingredients into one grocery list when planning several meals for the week.
indexExcerpt: Plan several meals and combine ingredients into one shopping-ready list.

sections.heading: Start with the dinners you need
sections.body: On Home, choose Plan my week. In Plan your week, choose how many days you need, the start date and servings. Choose Plan my week there to generate suggestions, then review the dinners, swap unsuitable meals or leave a day free. You can try this without an account or a saved recipe collection.

sections.heading: Keep the meals in one saved plan
sections.body: Choose Save my plan once the review looks right. Guests can review and swap meals before creating an account; signing in is needed to keep the plan and use its shopping list.

sections.heading: Review the automatically combined list
sections.body: Saving the plan creates one linked shopping list. Matching ingredient names are grouped, and compatible amounts can be added together. Different names may remain separate, and amounts with incompatible units are not automatically added together. Check the ingredient details before shopping rather than assuming every similar ingredient has been merged.

link.label: See the worked three-recipe shopping list, with quantities and source details.

sections.heading: Check what you already have
sections.body: Open an ingredient’s details to see the meals that need it. Check your cupboards yourself, then remove items you do not need to buy. Removed items can be restored if you change your mind.

sections.heading: Add the rest of your shop
sections.body: Add non-recipe essentials to the same list. If you swap a meal in the saved plan later, Foodedo updates the linked ingredients and keeps your manual extras. You do not need to rebuild the list.

title: Weekly Meal Plan and Shopping List Guide
excerpt: A repeatable weekly routine for planning meals, shopping once, and staying on track.
seoDescription: A repeatable weekly routine to review suggested dinners, save your meal plan and use its linked shopping list.
indexExcerpt: A repeatable weekly planning rhythm for households and families.

sections.heading: Pick one planning window each week
sections.body: Set aside a short time to check your calendar before shopping. Notice evenings when you will be out or need a simple dinner. The aim is a useful plan, not a perfectly filled week.

sections.heading: Review suggestions instead of starting from scratch
sections.body: On Home, choose Plan my week. In Plan your week, choose how many days you need, the start date and servings. Choose Plan my week there to generate suggestions, then review the dinners, swap unsuitable meals or leave a day free. You can try this without an account or a saved recipe collection.

sections.heading: Save your week and open Shopping
sections.body: Choose Save my plan when you are happy with the review. Sign in or create an account if you have been trying it as a guest. The saved plan creates its shopping list automatically. Open Shopping, remove ingredients already in your cupboards and add any extras you need.

link.label: See the worked three-recipe shopping list, with quantities and source details.

sections.heading: Set up a household when you want to share
sections.body: After signing in, use Share your week on Home to create a household and invite someone. They sign in and explicitly join using the invitation. Household members share that space’s plan and shopping list; Private remains a separate space. Select Household when you want to plan or shop together.

sections.heading: Adjust the plan when the week changes
sections.body: Swap a meal in the saved plan when your plans change; the linked shopping list updates with it. Check items off while shopping. Before planning the next week, think about which dinners were useful and which suggestions you would rather replace.

title: How to Build a Weekly Meal Plan in 15 Minutes
excerpt: A quick structure that helps you plan dinners fast without overthinking.
seoDescription: A practical 15-minute routine to create your weekly meal plan and stay realistic on busy days.
indexExcerpt: A quick routine for planning dinners when time is tight.

sections.heading: Minutes 1–3: check your week
sections.body: Look at your calendar and decide which evenings need dinner at home. Note busy nights and meals out. Treat this as a short routine to aim for, rather than a deadline for finding the perfect week.

sections.heading: Minutes 4–7: start with Foodedo’s suggestions
sections.body: On Home, choose Plan my week. In Plan your week, choose how many days you need, the start date and servings. Choose Plan my week there to generate suggestions, then review the dinners, swap unsuitable meals or leave a day free. You can try this without an account or a saved recipe collection.

sections.heading: Minutes 8–11: change only what needs changing
sections.body: Swap suggestions that do not suit your evenings, open recipes to check their ingredients or method, and leave a day free when you will not cook. Keep meals that already look useful instead of replacing every suggestion.

sections.heading: Minutes 12–15: save and prepare to shop
sections.body: Choose Save my plan. If you are a guest, sign in or create an account to keep it. Foodedo creates the linked shopping list automatically. Open Shopping, check what you already have, remove items you do not need and add everyday extras. Take more time if your week needs it.

title: How to Keep Meals Varied Without Overthinking It
excerpt: A realistic way to avoid repeats while keeping planning manageable.
seoDescription: Use a simple pattern to keep weekly meals varied without adding planning stress.
indexExcerpt: Avoid repeating the same meals with a simple weekly mix.

sections.heading: Start with a suggested mix
sections.body: On Home, choose Plan my week. In Plan your week, choose how many days you need, the start date and servings. Choose Plan my week there to generate suggestions, then review the dinners, swap unsuitable meals or leave a day free. You can try this without an account or a saved recipe collection.

sections.heading: Change one or two meals, not the whole week
sections.body: Keep suggestions that work and swap a meal where the week feels repetitive. Open the recipe to check its ingredients and method before choosing it. Small changes make variety easier to manage.

sections.heading: Look for different kinds of dinners
sections.body: Compare the recipes in your review: are they all similar dishes, or does the week offer a mix of ingredients and cooking styles? Choose a different meal through the swap options where you want a change. You do not have to rewrite recipe ingredients to get a different dinner.

sections.heading: Save the mix and let Shopping follow
sections.body: Choose Save my plan when you are happy with the week, signing in if you are a guest. The shopping list is created automatically. Later swaps in the saved plan update its linked ingredients, so your shop stays connected to the dinners you intend to cook.

title: Recipe App vs Meal Planner vs Grocery List App
excerpt: Most people need all three. The easiest setup is keeping recipes, planning, and shopping connected in one place.
seoDescription: What each tool does, where each one helps, and why connected meal planning plus grocery list tools are easier to maintain.
indexExcerpt: Compare tools and see why connected planning + shopping is easier.

sections.heading: Recipe apps help you find and keep ideas
sections.body: Recipes provide ingredients and cooking instructions. A collection can be useful, but having more recipes does not always make it easier to decide what to cook tonight or across a busy week.

sections.heading: Meal planners help you make the dinner decision
sections.body: A meal plan turns ideas into dinners. On Home, choose Plan my week. In Plan your week, choose how many days you need, the start date and servings. Choose Plan my week there to generate suggestions, then review the dinners, swap unsuitable meals or leave a day free. You can try this without an account or a saved recipe collection.

sections.heading: Shopping lists turn the decision into a shop
sections.body: A connected list uses the ingredients from your plan instead of making you copy each recipe into a note. In Foodedo, saving a plan creates its shopping list automatically, and changes to saved meals update the linked list.

sections.heading: Choose the sharing setup you actually need
sections.body: You can keep your saved plan and list private. If you want to cook or shop together, signed-in users can create a household and invite another person to join. Household and Private have separate plans and shopping lists; joining does not make everyone’s personal recipe library shared.

sections.heading: Try the decision before committing
sections.body: Choose Plan my week on Home, set up the days and servings, then generate and review suggestions as a guest. Choose Save my plan and sign in when you want to keep the week and use its shopping list. Check cupboards, remove ingredients you already have and add everyday extras directly in Shopping.
